newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish paint producer Meges floats part capital.
newsitem.headline: Turkish paint producer Meges floats part capital.

text.p: Turkish paint producer Meges Boya Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. floated shares representing a part of its capital in a two-day public offer beginning on Tuesday, the company said in newspaper advertisements.
The fixed price per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share is 6,200 lira in the offer managed by brokerage Finans Yatirim which is owned by Finansbank.
Of the total 50 million shares put on offer, 20 million are allocated to foreign investors, mutual funds, investment trusts and foundations based outside Turkey.

Meges, owned by Ercan Holding, produces water-based synthetic paints for use in industries and construction as well as insulation materials. It merged with its marketing arm last year to increase profitability.
It has some 400 outlets in Turkey and has a marketing company based in Moscow to sell its products to ex-Soviet republics.
Meges raised its net profits by 268 percent to 42 billion lira and net sales by 163 percent to 1.08 trillion lira in 1996 when compared to a year ago.
Its end-1997 targets are 275 billion lira of net profits and 2.5 trillion lira of turnover.
Meges whose sales in tonnes rose 10 percent last year, aims to increase its tonnage sales by 25 percent in 1997 with the help of newly completed paint investments.
The company said income from the public offer would be used to finance investment to introduce new production lines of industrial and synthetic paints and to improve productivity.
